rules.name: Application Information
rules.desc:
The Interdisciplinary Honors Program in Comparative Studies in Race and Ethnicity is intended to complement core curricular requirements in any major. Students who participate in the Interdisciplinary Honors Program receive their degree from their program of study with Interdisciplinary Honors in CSRE.
Honors applications are open to students who have a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall. Students in any major or program may apply to complete an honors project in CCSRE. See the "Required Preparatory Coursework" section below for additional course requirements required as part of the application process. These courses do not count towards the units required for completion of the Interdisciplinary Honors Program.
Applicants must submit a transcript and a project proposal. Before a proposal is submitted, the applicants’ proposed faculty advisor must review the proposal, offer feedback as appropriate, and confirm their willingness to supervise the project. The faculty advisor for an honors thesis in CCSRE must be an Academic Council faculty affiliate of CCSRE or a CCSRE Associate Director. Second readers may be Academic Council faculty members or any Stanford academic staff.
For more information about the Honors program and the application process, visit the Honors page on the CCSRE website.

rules.name: Required Honors Courses
rules.desc: CSRE honors students must enroll in CSRE 201X in the fall, 201Y in the winter, and 201Z in the spring, each of which must be taken for 5 units. These courses, which meet in person on a weekly basis, provide invaluable peer and faculty support to honors students as their projects unfold.

gpa: The Honors program is open to students with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall.
grading:
A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class toward the Core Curriculum.
A thesis must receive a grade of B+ or above for its author to receive honors in CSRE.
transferPolicy: No external credit may be applied toward the CSRE-IHN.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the preparatory coursework (CSRE 100 and one CCSRE core course, each with a C- or better) and the three honors seminars, CSRE 201X, 201Y and 201Z, at 5 units each. You check by hand the application GPA (3.7 in your major and 3.5 overall), the project proposal your faculty advisor reviews, and the B+ or better grade your thesis needs for honors.
